methodological_rigor.justification: Large prospective cohort study (n=1067) from INSCOC registry with systematic evaluation of 8 nutritional assessment tools. Comprehensive data collection from multiple Chinese institutions 2013-2021. Rigorous exclusion criteria applied; multivariate Cox regression, LASSO variable selection, time-dependent AUC analyses performed. However, limited to observational association; no causal inference. Subgroup analysis (leukemia vs. lymphoma) underpowered for leukemia. No pre-specified analysis plan mentioned.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Observational cohort (LoE 2b) evaluating prognostic value of nutritional assessment tools in hematologic malignancies. Clinical relevance moderate: identifies that existing tools (PG-SGA, NRS-2002, GLIM) show limited discrimination (AUC 0.47-0.56) in this population, particularly leukemia (all AUCs <0.55, essentially random). Proposes modified tool (HMPG-SGA) with improved AUC 0.616. Addresses unmet need for hematologic-specific nutritional prognostication but mechanism unclear.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows STROBE principles for observational cohort; baseline characteristics clearly presented (Table 1). Multiple nutritional assessment approaches systematically described (Supplementary Tables). Primary outcome (OS) and secondary outcomes (LOS, EORTC QLQ-C30) defined. Multivariate analyses with appropriate statistical methods. However, INSCOC registry registration referenced but link redacted; no mention of data repository or code availability for LASSO models or modified tool derivation.

novelty_literature.justification: First study to systematically evaluate 8 nutritional assessment tools in hematologic malignancies using multidimensional statistical modeling. Identifies critical gap: conventional tools developed for solid tumors show poor discrimination in leukemia/lymphoma. Novel approach integrating hematologic biomarkers (NLR, PAR, AGR) into modified PG-SGA framework (HMPG-SGA). Meaningful contribution but tool development preliminary; external validation lacking.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written manuscript clearly articulating biological rationale for hematologic-specific assessment (bone marrow involvement, systemic inflammation, immune dysfunction distinct from solid tumors). Introduction contextualizes unmet need effectively. Methods comprehensively describe 8 tools and 10 biomarkers examined. Results systematically compare predictive performance. Discussion insightfully explains discrepancy from solid tumor literature (rapid progression in leukemia, disease-driven malnutrition). Effective use of supplementary figures.

key_strengths: Large prospective cohort (1067 patients, 696 lymphoma, 371 leukemia) with long-term follow-up from INSCOC registry
Systematic evaluation of 8 commonly-used nutritional assessment tools with transparent reporting of limited discrimination (AUC range 0.47-0.56)
Clear identification of major finding: conventional tools show essentially random performance in leukemia (max AUC 0.544, comparable to coin flip)
Biologically motivated development of HMPG-SGA incorporating hematologic indicators (NLR, PAR, AGR) with improved performance (AUC 0.616 vs. 0.547 for original PG-SGA)
Subgroup analyses demonstrating differential tool performance (better in lymphoma than leukemia)
key_concerns: Modified tool (HMPG-SGA) development and validation performed in same cohort; no independent external validation provided; high risk of overfitting
LASSO regression variable selection from 10 biomarkers with small event numbers (total OS events not explicitly stated) risks unstable estimates
Clinical utility of HMPG-SGA unclear: improvement from AUC 0.547 to 0.616 remains modest; C-index 0.605 indicates only moderate predictive discrimination
Mechanism linking hematologic biomarkers to nutritional status not mechanistically validated; causality speculative
Subgroup analysis limited by small numbers and lack of statistical power; leukemia findings essentially negative (all tools AUC <0.55)
INSCOC registry link redacted; reproducibility limited by lack of data sharing or code availability for complex LASSO-based tool derivation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Addresses genuine clinical gap (poor performance of solid-tumor-derived tools in hematologic cancers) with sound methods, but modified tool development lacks external validation and shows only modest improvement. Appropriate for Tier 3 (competent observational work with incremental methodological contribution). Major revisions needed: independent validation cohort, mechanistic justification, clinical implementation guidance, and transparent code sharing.
